{"self_assessment": "Impact: Our table built a fish and, by the last check, about 244 of 249 standing dominoes were connected to the start, so nearly the whole picture fell. My part was laying dominoes onto the top line from around the upper tail lobe and checking the body, belly and tail fork for gaps. I laid roughly a dozen dominoes there. I also inspected several areas, which showed me no breaks I needed to fix.

Execution: I worked in short batches on the top line and stood one fallen domino back up. I inspected the body and tail at several points (about 3:00, 5:00, 5:15, 5:45 and 6:15). I stayed off the start domino and kept my hands off the tail and body once the table agreed to freeze them. That kept the connected run intact up to the push.

Collaboration: I asked early whether the tail was its own stroke, so I understood the plan before building. I offered to take the top line and then waited for Hana's go-ahead so we wouldn't double up on it. I kept my hands off areas others were working in, and I gave credit to Sofia, Omar and Hana as the work came together.

Leadership: I'm not claiming a leadership role at this table. Hana set the animal and the stroke plan. What I did was support it: I confirmed roles out loud, checked in before touching shared areas, and encouraged the team in the final minutes. My contribution was real but smaller than the others'. I'd put it at about a tenth of the result.", "my_share_percent": 10}
